newsitem.title: USA: U.N. says talks on Iraq aid plan set for Sunday.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says talks on Iraq aid plan set for Sunday.

text.p: The United Nations humanitarian coordinator in Iraq, Staffan de Mistura, will meet with Iraqi officials on Sunday for further talks on Baghdad's aid distribution plan, a U.N. spokeswoman said.

Iraqi officials gave de Mistura a preliminary draft plan for aid distribution on Wednesday, which the U.N. official said still needed some work before it can be presented to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

The Secretary-General must approve the plan in order to restart oil exports under the "oil-for-food" scheme which allows Baghdad an exemption to broader sanctions to alleviate suffering of ordinary Iraqis.
Oil exports under the scheme began on December 10 and ran initially for 180 days. The deal was renewed from June 8 but exports have been stalled pending receipt of a new distribution plan.
Iraq's oil minister said two weeks ago that he expected oil exports to begin in seven to 10 days, give or take a few days, at a rate of around 730,000 to 750,000 barrels per day (bpd).
